title: Emergency throttle & rehire sinewave — headcount and price sensitivity notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
---
Working notes for an emergency throttle + rehire "sinewave" protocol: a light-weight, trigger-driven set of actions that (a) slows external capacity consumption when price/usage deteriorates, (b) temporarily re-prioritizes hiring and contractor usage to maintain SLAs, and (c) defines quick pricing levers to preserve margin while minimizing long-term churn.

Status: draft; this is intentionally operational (checklist + triggers) rather than a polished strategy doc. Meant for finance, platform ops, and SRE on-call coordination.

Background / why this exists:
- We observed two fast shocks in 2026: 1) a regional customer burst doubled on-demand GPU hours for ~48h; 2) a multi-week enterprise pipeline test increased average sequence length and token mix, pushing unit cost up ~35%.
- Our current ramp/hire cadence is too sticky for short shocks. Need a reversible policy that lets us compress labor and ephemeral capacity quickly, then unwind without breaking customer trust.

Design principles:
- Non-binary: avoid all-or-nothing layoffs or blanket price hikes. Favor small increments and multi-stage rollbacks.
- Signal-driven: triggers should map to measurable signals (token cost/gpu-hour, 7d retention, route error rate).
- Customer fairness: prioritize customers on committed tiers and safety-critical flows.
- Short half-life: any temporary measures should be designed to fully unwind inside 8–12 weeks.

Signals and thresholds (proposal):
1) Token-cost index (TCI): our internal rolling 7d effective cost-per-1k-tokens (includes GPU spot/commit mix + quantization adjustments).
   - Green: TCI <= baseline * 1.05 (no action).
   - Amber: TCI > baseline * 1.05 && <= baseline * 1.20 (start soft throttle + hiring freeze).
   - Red: TCI > baseline * 1.20 (activate hard throttle + limited rehire reprioritization).
2) Queue latency SLO breach frequency: > 3% of routes in 24h -> consider temporary reassign of dedicated pools to high-priority routes.
3) Committed revenue delta: if forecasted committed MRR drop > 2% in 14d due to customer churn signals, trigger conservative price tilt for new provisioning.

Operational actions by stage:
- Amber (soft):
  * Freeze all non-critical external contractor starts (stop offer acceptance where start_date > 21 days).
  * Pause 40% of non-customer-facing hires + delay internal tools hiring by one sprint.
  * Reduce new on-demand GPU procurement (spot bids) by 30% and move new requests to queued burst pool.
  * Pricing experiment: increase trial seat token price by +7% for new signups only (A/B test 50/50).
  * Start a 2-week sprint to reduce non-essential batch workloads (jobs flagged 'batch-low-priority').
- Red (hard):
  * Halt all open reqs except critical SRE/infra/committed-account coverage.
  * Convene exec 24h + notify sales/customer success of potential limited throttling for non-committed routes.
  * Activate capacity rebalancer: move 60% of ephemeral capacity to committed-customer pools.
  * Apply temporary 10–15% price uplift on pay-as-you-go token tiers with a 14-day notice to customers (opt-out allowed for committed contracts).
  * Short-term contractor rehire: convert 50% of contractor pipeline to 90d fixed engagements (cheaper hourly + flexible end).

Quick math (illustrative assumptions):
- Baseline monthly GPU spend (on-demand + spot): $1.9M. Baseline committed cost offset: $700k (reserved). Effective baseline net GPU cost = $1.2M/month.
- If token mix increases (longer sequences) raising TCI by 20% => expected incremental burn ~ $240k/month.
- Amber steps target ~40–60% of that incremental burn via throttles + pause on new hires (~$100–150k/mo).
- Red steps target ~80–100% of incremental burn (~$190–240k/mo) while preserving committed coverage.

Mini-scenario table (text table):
Scenario | Headcount delta (3mo) | Expected monthly savings | Pricing shift (new customers)
Baseline | +2 FTE net | $0 | 0%
Amber | -4 hires paused, +0 FTE reduction (delay) | $120k | +7% A/B test (new signups)
Red | -6 hires deferred, 2 contractors converted to fixed | $220k | +12% uplift for PAYG new customers

Risks / mitigations:
- Customer backlash: coordinate CS with a playbook and 72h pre-notify if shifting capacity. Provide credits for impacted committed customers.
- Hiring morale: keep transparent timelines and prefer slowdowns over rescinds. Use redeployment/postpone options rather than cancel offers when possible.
- SLA slippage: explicit SLO prioritization; do not throttle high-priority or security-critical APIs.

Open questions:
- How do we define baseline TCI for model upgrades (if we onboard a quantized model that permanently reduces cost, baseline must shift)? Action: Product + Research define model-based baseline migration rule (P0).
- Do we want a soft-cooldown for new paid customers (e.g., throttle trials harder than enterprise)? Need legal check on differential pricing notices.
- Should we pre-authorize a small emergency credit pool for customers impacted by throttles? Ops + Finance to propose $Xk pool.

Immediate next steps (owners & timeline):
- Finance: produce a daily TCI dashboard (TCI, cost-per-seq, GPU-hour) by 2026-11-09 — owner: Priya.
- Platform Ops: implement a soft-throttle label and routing rule in the rebalancer (ETA 2026-11-16) — owner: Liam.
- People Ops: draft candidate communication templates for paused offers (ETA 2026-11-12) — owner: Riley.
- Legal: sign off on short-term trial-price uplift notice language (ETA 2026-11-14).

Quick checklist for on-call (starter):
- [ ] Verify TCI feed and compare with baseline multiplier.
- [ ] If Amber -> run "soft-throttle" tag script (ops/rebalancer/soft_throttle_v2).
- [ ] If Red -> escalate to Finance-Exec channel + invoke pricing uplift playbook.
- [ ] Notify CS for top 10 committed customers if capacity moves.

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Consider a 3-week rolling window rather than strict 7d smoothing for TCI to avoid reaction to microbursts.
- Keep 2–3 contractors pre-approved for rapid rehiring in case we need to restore capacity fast — cheaper than long onboarding.
- Watch GPU spot market for index spikes (alerts when spot > 1.6x median of last 30d).

Appendix A: short commands + spreadsheet pointers (operational)
- Cost model repo: github.com/redwood-inference/cost-models (run scripts/calc_tci.py --window 7 --output daily.csv)
- Quick workbook: /drive/finance/quick-sims/emergency-throttle-sim.xlsx (internal pointer — finance notebook).

End of draft.

Comments welcome — please add inline notes or post to #finance-ops for rapid iteration.
